passages.text: Before Meituan, Wang built and lost control of a Facebook clone called Xiaonei (later rebranded Renren after being sold due to financial problems) and founded microblogging site Fanfou in 2007, which was shut down by the government.

Wang holds a bachelor's degree in electronic engineering from Tsinghua University and pursued but did not complete a PhD in computer engineering at the University of Delaware, leaving with a master's degree instead.

Wang's repeated early failures (Duoduoyou, Youzitu, losing control of Xiaonei, the government shutdown of Fanfou) preceded his eventual success founding Meituan in 2010, reflecting a multi-attempt entrepreneurial path rather than a single breakthrough.
Meituan grew into a dominant Chinese local-services and food-delivery platform, with Wang continuing as CEO as of the source's most recent update.

Wang Xing belongs to Group 4 - Mobile/e-commerce. The mobile/e-commerce group covers founders who built the smartphone-era platforms of the 2010s — ride-hailing (Didi), social commerce (Pinduoduo), local services (Meituan), short video (Kuaishou), logistics (SF Express, ZTO), and e-commerce at scale (JD.com) — a cohort whose businesses were shaped by the mobile-internet transition and, for several, by the 2020-2021 regulatory tightening.
